boundary: Synthetic 25-month canonical evaluation only. Not the hospital's retention schedule, not a legal determination, and not an approval of real staff data. Values were fixed from category semantics before any reviewed 25-month run and must not be tuned to its outcome.

retention_rules.purpose: Synthetic protocol: superseded scheduling drafts, jobs, inputs and receipts
Synthetic protocol: operational event outbox and notification reads
Synthetic protocol: working-time and leave records (placeholder, facility rule unconfirmed)
Synthetic protocol: staff identity and membership records (placeholder, facility rule unconfirmed)
Synthetic protocol: privacy request case records

typed_parent_relations.precedence: a matching planning_outbox typed event relation replaces the generic top-level parent

approve_only_if: source row exists and its jsonb sha256 equals the registered content hash
scope is the reviewed facility scope (never __unclassified__)
independently extracted structured subject set equals the registered subject set and contains the requested person
no known person identifier or registered name occurs in any unstructured string value

typed_actor_accounts.resolution: account_memberships.subject equals the value (active or inactive); membership scope equals the row scope unless the row scope is missing/__unclassified__; issuer must match when the object carries an issuer
typed_actor_accounts.excluded_from_unstructured_scan: only when the value resolved to at least one membership in the row scope

database_subject_review.name_exemption: a name value is exempt only when it is a registered name of the person_id in the same object
database_subject_review.verified_status_trust: only this protocol hash reviewer evidence bound to the current content hash; otherwise independently re-checked and re-recorded

approve_only_if: subject review of the row is VERIFIED
no owner of the row is under an active legal hold
no other owner already has an approved erasure control (joint review is required instead)
projection adapter is partial-planning-history-v1 and its payload hash is the one reviewed
the projected payload retains no occurrence of the erased person's identifier or name
the application exposes a joint-review context for the copy (all owners approved and controlled, no hold, retention expired)
the file on disk hashes to the context source hash
the reviewer parses the snapshot itself: its people set equals the registered owners and the context owners
every owner has an approved erasure control (ErasedSubject) in the facility
no known person identifier outside the owners occurs anywhere in the snapshot text
the reviewer read the whole shared text and records shared_text_reviewed

supersedes.observation: Independent review found that v2 skipped every typed actor value in the unstructured scan even when unresolved, skipped any name next to a person_id, trusted application-set VERIFIED status, and approved joint file erasure without the reviewer comparing the snapshot people itself.
supersedes.change: Stricter only. Actor values are exempt from the unstructured scan only when they resolved to a membership in the row scope; a name is exempt only when it is a registered name of that object person_id; VERIFIED is trusted only with this protocol hash own reviewer evidence bound to the current content hash, otherwise the row is independently re-checked; joint file approval requires the reviewer own comparison of snapshot people, registered owners, context owners and each owner approved control, plus no unregistered known token. Retention values are unchanged. v1/v2 and their results are retained.
